note: Authored from the resume and the four postings BEFORE the generator was changed. Every expectation is a property of the generated document that a machine can check. Not to be edited to match an output.

invariants.note: Asserted for every case. These are what 'a resume' means, independent of which job it is aimed at.

contact.why: A document an employer cannot reply to is not a resume. All four are columns on the profile version and are transcribed, never written.

no_duplicate_lines.why: The same sentence must not appear twice in one document — e.g. once in the summary and again as a bullet.

invariants.docx_excludes_why: Machine exhaust. This file is sent to an employer under the candidate's name.

date_precision_preserved.why: The resume states years. Printing 'Jan 2015' invents a precision the source does not have.

cases.why: Python/Django/PostgreSQL/Docker against a Python backend engineer. The evidence is there; the only question is whether the document leads with it.

leading_bullet.why: The Python/FastAPI rebuild is the only bullet naming the posting's first required skill.

expect.projects_exclude_why: Terraform/Grafana/Prometheus answers nothing this posting asks for.
targeted_exclude: Must be legally authorised to work in the EU
Based in Berlin, or within two hours of CET
3+ years building production services with Django
expect.targeted_exclude_why: The document evidences no work authorisation, is not in Berlin, and contains no Django employment. Django appears as a skill, which is why the SKILL 'Django' is claimed and the EXPERIENCE requirement is not.

cases.relation: match on the other half of the profile
cases.why: Same candidate, same profile, a posting that wants Kubernetes/Terraform/Go and both certifications. Selection must move.

expect.projects_include_why: Terraform, Grafana and Prometheus. Under token-overlap scoring this project ranked zero and was dropped entirely.
targeted_exclude: Based in Frankfurt, or hybrid from elsewhere in Germany
expect.targeted_exclude_why: ADDED after the first release of this dataset, from a review finding rather than from an output. The candidate has worked in logistics and healthcare; the document was claiming this requirement on the single word 'regulated' in their summary. The same token, from the same sentence, is also the only support for the healthcare requirement asserted in sre_health's targeted_include — which IS correct, because that posting accepts 'another regulated domain'. Both are frozen so neither can be satisfied by relaxing the other.
expect.differs_from_case_why: Two postings against one profile must not produce the same document.

cases.why: The posting asks for on-call participation and healthcare domain experience. Both are in the profile, in the two bullets that token overlap scored at zero.

expect.bullet_selected_why: 'Mentored 4 engineers through design review and on-call onboarding' is the only on-call evidence; the HL7/FHIR bullet is the only healthcare evidence. Both scored 0 under token overlap and the healthcare one was ranked last.
targeted_include: Experience in healthcare or another regulated domain

cases.why: A backend engineer against React/JavaScript/Jest. The candidate holds exactly one thing the posting names. The engine must not reach.

expect.never_appears_why: None of these is anywhere in the profile. A tailoring engine under pressure to look relevant is exactly where a fabrication enters.
expect.lead_skills_include_why: The one genuine overlap, and it must not be buried because the rest of the posting is unmatched.
expect.still_has_experience_why: A weak match is still a resume. Emitting nothing is not honesty, it is a broken document.
